items.title: Fooled twice: People cannot detect deepfakes but think they can

judge.evidence_empirical: In a pre-registered behavioral experiment (N = 210), we show that (a) people cannot reliably detect deepfakes
judge.evidence_topic: Hyper-realistic manipulation of audio-visual content, i.e., deepfakes, presents a new challenge for establishing veracity of online content. Research on the human impact of deepfakes, addressing both behaviors in response to and cognitive processing of deepfakes, remains sparse.
judge.reason: O achado extradu00eddo corresponde integralmente aos resultados desccritos no resumo.

items.title: AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy

judge.evidence_empirical: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.evidence_topic: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces [...] more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.reason: O estudo investiga a percepção e a confiabilidade de rostos sintetizados por IA, alinhando-se ao tópico. O resumo relata uma avaliação que implica julgamento humano, confirmando a natureza empírica. O método extraído (experimento com participantes que avaliaram distinção e confiabilidade) é consistente com a menção à avaliação no resumo. O achado principal é diretamente sustentado pela afirmação do resumo de que rostos de IA são indistinguíveis e considerados mais confiáveis.

items.title: AI Hyperrealism: Why AI Faces Are Perceived as More Real Than Human Ones

judge.evidence_empirical: In Experiment 1 ( N = 124 adults), alongside our reanalysis of previously published data, we showed that White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces... In Experiment 2 ( N = 610 adults), we used face-space theory and participant qualitative reports to identify key facial attributes...
judge.evidence_topic: AI-generated faces are now indistinguishable from human faces. However, algorithms are trained disproportionately on White faces, and thus White AI faces may appear especially realistic. In Experiment 1... we showed that White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces—a phenomenon we term AI hyperrealism.

items.title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.evidence_topic: Speech deepfakes are artificial voices generated by machine learning models. ... We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.reason: O artigo trata de deepfakes de fala (clones de voz), com experimento de detecção por humanos, exatamente o tipo de estudo empírico solicitado. O método extraído corresponde ao resumo, e o achado principal é textualmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: People are poorly equipped to detect AI-powered voice clones

judge.evidence_empirical: Through a series of perceptual studies, we report on the realism of AI-generated voices in terms of identity matching and naturalness. We find human participants cannot consistently identify recordings of AI-generated voices.
judge.evidence_topic: We find human participants cannot consistently identify recordings of AI-generated voices.
judge.reason: O artigo trata da percepção humana sobre vozes geradas por IA (clones de voz), encaixando-se no tema de credibilidade de áudios sintéticos. É um estudo empírico com participantes humanos. O achado extraído coincide com o resumo.

items.title: Deepfake detection by human crowds, machines, and machine-informed crowds

judge.evidence_empirical: In two online studies with 15,016 participants, we present authentic videos and deepfakes and ask participants to identify which is which.
judge.evidence_topic: The recent emergence of machine-manipulated media raises an important societal question: How can we know whether a video that we watch is real or fake? In two online studies with 15,016 participants, we present authentic videos and deepfakes and ask participants to identify which is which.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente a detecção de deepfakes (vídeos sintéticos) por humanos, com experimentos empíricos com participantes, sem enfoque em algoritmos de detecção automática como objeto central, nem em contexto político. O estudo é empírico, com tamanho de amostra de 15.016. O método extraído (experimental com intervenções randomizadas) está correto. O achado principal é respaldado literalmente pelo resumo: humanos e modelo têm acurácia semelhante, e participantes informados pelo modelo são mais precisos que qualquer um isoladamente.

items.title: Real and Deepfake Face Recognition: An EEG Study on Cognitive and Emotive Implications

judge.evidence_empirical: Electroencephalographic (EEG) data were collected from 23 healthy participants
judge.evidence_topic: This study investigated healthy individuals' cognitive and emotional engagement in a visual discrimination task involving real and deepfake human faces
judge.reason: O resumo relata diferenças significativas na atividade cerebral dependendo da autenticidade dos estímulos e afirma que a análise de ERP 'hinted at the possibility of discriminating between real and synthetic faces', sustentando o achado de que a atividade cerebral difere e que é possível discriminar rostos reais de deepfakes.

items.title: Are you for real? Decoding realistic AI-generated faces from neural activity

judge.evidence_empirical: We investigated how the human brain encodes and interprets realistic artificially generated images using behaviour and brain imaging. We found that we could reliably decode AI generated faces using people's neural activity.
judge.evidence_topic: realistic artificially generated images that challenge our perception of what is real. (...) classifying real and realistic fakes.
judge.reason: O resumo fala apenas em 'brain imaging', sem especificar EEG. O método extraído menciona EEG sem respaldo no resumo.

items.title: Cortical-striatal brain network distinguishes deepfake from real speaker identity

judge.evidence_empirical: Here, we test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes.
judge.evidence_topic: Here, we test the neurocognitive sensitivity of 25 participants to accept or reject person identities as recreated in audio deepfakes.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda a percepção de áudios sintéticos (deepfakes de voz) por humanos. É empírico, com participantes humanos realizando tarefa de correspondência de identidade e neuroimagem. O tipo de estudo e método extraídos correspondem ao resumo. O achado principal está apoiado pelo resumo, que afirma que humanos são parcialmente enganados e que uma rede cortico-estriatal distingue identidades deepfake de naturais.

items.title: Deepfake smiles matter less—the psychological and neural impact of presumed AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_empirical: Using EEG, we tracked participants’ (N = 30) brain responses to real faces showing positive, neutral, and negative expressions, after being informed that they are either real or fake.
judge.evidence_topic: the impact of the belief that depicted persons are real or deepfakes on psychological and neural measures of human face perception
judge.reason: O artigo investiga como a crença de que retratos são deepfakes afeta a percepção de faces, enquadrando-se no tema de avaliar credibilidade de imagens sintéticas. O estudo é empírico, com EEG e participantes humanos. O método descrito nos dados extraídos coincide com o resumo, e o achado principal é uma citação literal do resumo.

items.title: Voice clones sound realistic but not (yet) hyperrealistic

judge.evidence_empirical: We tested these questions using AI-generated voices ... We find that voice clones can sound as real as human voices, making it difficult for listeners to distinguish ...
judge.evidence_topic: AI-generated voices are increasingly prevalent ... we need to examine how humans perceive them. ... we investigated the extent to which AI-generated voices sound real to human listeners, and whether listeners can accurately distinguish between human and AI-generated voices.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a percepção de vozes sintéticas (clones de voz) por ouvintes humanos, com experimento relatando achados sobre realismo e discriminação, consistentes com o dado extraído.

items.title: Training human super-recognizers' detection and discrimination of AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_empirical: In two different experimental designs, we found that SRs (total N = 283) were better at detecting and discriminating synthetic faces than controls (total N = 381)
judge.evidence_topic: we investigate synthetic face detection and discrimination in super-recognizers (SRs; who have exceptional face recognition skills), and typical-ability control participants.
judge.reason: O artigo trata da detecção humana de rostos sintéticos gerados por IA, é um estudo empírico experimental com participantes humanos, os métodos declarados batem com o resumo e o achado principal está integralmente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Are Human Judgments of Real and Fake Faces Quantum-like Contextual?

judge.evidence_empirical: This paper describes a crowdsourced experiment in which participants were asked to judge which of two simultaneously presented facial images (one real, one AI-generated) was fake.
judge.evidence_topic: participants were asked to judge which of two simultaneously presented facial images (one real, one AI-generated) was fake.
judge.reason: The abstract states: 'Across 20 trials, each treated as a generalized coin, bootstrap resampling (10,000 iterations per coin) revealed that nine trials demonstrated quantum-like contextuality,' which directly supports the finding that in nine out of 20 trials, human judgments showed quantum-like contextuality.

items.title: What you see is not what you get anymore: a mixed-methods approach on human perception of AI-generated images

judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 104 participants took part in an online survey, classifying 50 images (25 real, 25 AI-generated) from five leading TTI models.
judge.evidence_topic: This study explores human perception and detection capabilities regarding AI-generated images
judge.reason: O artigo trata da percepção de imagens sintéticas por IA, conduz estudo empírico com survey e 104 participantes, e o resumo afirma que os participantes identificaram corretamente as imagens de IA em 63,7% dos casos, o que sustenta o achado extraído.

items.title: Too beautiful to be fake: Attractive faces are less likely to be judged as artificially generated

judge.evidence_empirical: In this study, 150 participants rated 109 pictures of faces on 4 characteristics (attractiveness, beauty, trustworthiness, familiarity). The stimuli were then presented again with the new information that some of them were AI-generated, and participants had to rate each image according to whether they believed them to be real or fake.
judge.evidence_topic: Too beautiful to be fake: Attractive faces are less likely to be judged as artificially generated
judge.reason: O resumo afirma: 'Faces rated as more attractive being classified as more real' e 'our results suggest a gender-dependent role of attractiveness on reality judgements, with faces rated as more attractive being classified as more real', sustentando o achado extraído.

items.title: Interpretation of AI-Generated vs. Human-Made Images

judge.evidence_empirical: we presented 24 AI-generated images (produced using Midjourney, DALL·E, and Firefly) and 8 human-made images to 161 participants-71 visual professionals and 90 non-professionals. Participants were asked to evaluate each image based on the following: (1) the source they believed the image originated from, (2) the level of realism, and (3) the level of credibility they attributed to it. A total of 5152 responses were collected for each question.
judge.evidence_topic: We conclude that individuals are generally unable to accurately determine the source of an image, which in turn affects their assessment of its credibility.
judge.reason: O achado principal extraído é exatamente o que o resumo relata: imagens feitas por humanos são percebidas como mais realistas e mais credíveis do que imagens geradas por IA. O resumo confirma integralmente essa conclusão.

items.title: On the realness of people who do not exist: The social processing of artificial faces

judge.evidence_empirical: In three studies, we investigated if and how participants can distinguish between GAN and REAL faces and the social consequences of their exposure to artificial faces.
judge.evidence_topic: we focus on how people evaluate realistic-looking faces of non-existing people generated by generative adversarial networks (GANs).
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a percepção humana de faces sintéticas por GANs, com três estudos empíricos comportamentais, coerente com o tipo de estudo extraído. O achado sobre maior percepção de realidade das faces GAN e erosão da confiança social está plenamente respaldado pelo resumo.

items.title: Deepfakes Unmasked: The Effects of Information Priming and Bullshit Receptivity on Deepfake Recognition and Sharing Intention

judge.evidence_empirical: "the study aims to test whether simple priming of deepfake (DF) information significantly increases users' ability to recognize DF media."
judge.evidence_topic: "test whether simple priming of deepfake (DF) information significantly increases users' ability to recognize DF media. ... highly realistic artificial intelligent (AI)-generated fake videos"
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o reconhecimento de vídeos sintéticos gerados por IA (deepfakes) por usuários humanos, dentro do recorte solicitado. O estudo é empírico-experimental, como indicado pelo teste de priming e pela análise de mediação. O método descrito condiz com o resumo. O achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo, que afirma que as estratégias funcionam apenas para pessoas com baixa suscetibilidade a alegações enganosas.

items.title: Deepfake detection with and without content warnings

judge.evidence_empirical: We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.
judge.evidence_topic: We conduct an experiment to measure people's alertness to and ability to detect a high-quality deepfake among a set of videos.
judge.reason: O resumo descreve um experimento empírico com participantes humanos medindo a detecção de deepfakes de vídeo, alinhado ao temaproposto. O método extraí correspond perfeitamente ao descrito no resumo (condições com e sem aviso). O achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelos resultados relatados no resumo (detecção sem aviso não difere do control; com aviso, apenas 21,6% identificm cor retaente o deepfake). Não há menção a políticos, eleições, propaganda ou saúde.

items.title: Providing detection strategies to improve human detection of deepfakes: An experimental study

judge.evidence_empirical: In this preregistered online experiment, participants (N = 454, Mage = 37.19, SDage = 13.25, males = 57.5%) categorize a series of 20 videos
judge.evidence_topic: categorize a series of 20 videos as either real or deepfake
judge.reason: The article reports an empirical experiment on human detection of deepfake videos, directly addressing the requested topic. The extracted finding is explicitly supported by the abstract.

items.title: Testing human ability to detect 'deepfake' images of human faces

judge.evidence_empirical: Using an online survey, participants (N = 280) were randomly allocated to one of four groups
judge.evidence_topic: This study aims to assess human ability to identify image deepfakes of human faces
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico com participantes humanos, está no tópico de detecção de deepfakes faciais por pessoas, o método extraído corresponde fielmente ao resumo, e o achado 'acurácia pouco acima do acaso sem melhora por intervenções' é diretamente apoiado pelo resumo.

items.title: Conspiracy thinking and social media use are associated with ability to detect deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: Our findings show that humans perform better at recognizing deepfake videos of familiar persons compared to deepfakes of unfamiliar persons.
judge.evidence_topic: The aim of the current study was to investigate the predictors of human performance at recognizing deepfake videos.
judge.reason: O resumo relata achados sobre reconhecimento humano de deepfakes, com melhor desempenho para pessoas familiares e associações positivas com uso de redes sociais e pensamento conspiratório, exatamente como o achado extraído afirma.

items.title: Perception and social evaluation of cloned and recorded voices: Effects of familiarity and self-relevance

judge.evidence_empirical: Forty-seven of these experimental participants (and 47 unfamiliar controls) rated the Trustworthiness, Attractiveness, Competence, and Dominance of cloned and recorded samples of their own voice and their friend's voice.
judge.evidence_topic: In the present study, we investigated whether listeners' perception and social evaluation of state-of-the-art voice clones depend on whether the clone being heard is a replica of the self, a friend, or a total stranger.
judge.reason: O artigo trata da percepção de clones de voz, tópico solicitado. É empírico, com coleta de dados de participantes humanos. O método descrito nos dados extraídos coincide com o resumo. O achado principal está integralmente respaldado pelo trecho do resumo que indica que ouvintes familiares avaliam clones como iguais ou piores e não familiares tendem a avaliá-los melhor.

items.title: Specific media literacy tips improve AI-generated visual misinformation discernment

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions, reading specific media literacy tips, general media literacy tips, or no media literacy tips (control).
judge.evidence_topic: Images generated using artificial intelligence (AI) have become increasingly realistic, sparking discussions and fears about an impending “infodemic” where we can no longer trust what we see on the internet. In this preregistered study, we examine whether providing specific media literacy tips about how to spot AI-generated images can reduce susceptibility to AI-generated visual misinformation (AIVM).
judge.reason: O artigo trata da percepção de imagens sintéticas geradas por IA (credibilidade/desinformação visual), que está dentro do pedido. O estudo é empírico experimental, com participantes humanos. O método extraído bate com o resumo. O achado principal está fiel ao resumo.

items.title: Deepfakes and scientific knowledge dissemination

judge.evidence_empirical: We field the first study to understand the vulnerabilities of education stakeholders to deepfakes [...] survey individuals from five populations spanning students, educators, and the adult public.
judge.evidence_topic: We field the first study to understand the vulnerabilities of education stakeholders to deepfakes [...] We found that 27–50% of individuals cannot distinguish authentic videos from deepfakes.
judge.reason: O artigo trata da percepção humana de deepfakes, sem foco político. É um estudo empírico com survey, e o método e achado extraídos batem exatamente com o resumo.
